title: Initialized DATA implies SAVE — local variable persists between calls
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE NEXT_TICKET(NUM)
C     Returns a monotonically-increasing ticket number, starting at
C     1 on the first call. The COUNTER is initialised via DATA which
C     by F77 standard implies SAVE -- COUNTER retains its value
C     across calls even without an explicit SAVE statement.
C     A naive rewrite that allocates COUNTER on the stack per
C     invocation will produce 1 every time.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER NUM
      INTEGER COUNTER
      DATA    COUNTER /0/

      COUNTER = COUNTER + 1
      NUM     = COUNTER
      RETURN
      END
notes:
The F77 standard says DATA-initialised locals are implicitly SAVE.
IBM XL Fortran honoured this. GCC's gfortran honours it. Some
modernised compilers and a naive Java/C# translation do not, so
the rewrite loses the monotonic-counter behaviour. The extract
pipeline MUST flag the cross-call state preservation; the open
question on concurrency is also material -- F77 has no thread
story so the rewrite has to make one explicit.
